attributes.title: Junior Client Success Manager
attributes.description:
• Fluent written and spoken English. Our clients are US doctors. You will write to them and speak with them every day.
  • You own outcomes. You have handled client relationships and can tell us what you kept, what you lost and why. Haven't owned a client book yet? tell us honestly.
  • You bring bad news early, with a plan. You do not wait to be asked.
  • You write clearly and fast. If your writing needs a second pass to be understood, this is the wrong seat.
  • You can hold a doctor's respect. Calm, direct, prepared, unbothered by pushback.
  • You live in AI tools. You useClaude or similar every day, can show us how, and pick up new tools fast. This matters more to us than your resume.

You do not need to be a GoHighLevel expert on day one, but you must learn fast and be willing to build. You need to work 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM US Eastern, with your camera on.

Skunks on the table

Every line is true. If one makes you want to close the tab, that is useful for both of us. If they make you lean in, you are probably who we are looking for.

  • This is a fully remote position. If you do not have a quiet, productive place to work from home with reliable power and internet, this is not the right role for you.
  • Going quiet is the one thing that does not work here. Missed a deadline? Tell us. Stuck? Say "I hit a wall." Problems get named the same day, in the open.
  • No recipe, and the structure keeps moving. We are "building the plane while flying it," and pods, seats and clients change as we grow. The first 2 to 3 weeks are quiet. The people who thrive start digging before anyone asks.
  • The CEO is direct. Plain feedback, expected back. He loves being challenged and hates silence.
  • Doctors push back, and quality beats volume. Our clients are smart, busy and spending their own money, so you hold your ground with evidence. A cheap lead who cannot afford a $4,000 treatment is not a win. Compliance is non-negotiable: no guarantees, no definitive claims.
  • You are the last set of eyes. Errors that should have been caught in QA come out of the pod's bonus pool, just as retention and expansion grow it.

Our values: give a shit · better before bigger · sincere candor · move fast and fix it · prove it works · unimpeachable character.
attributes.projects:
WANTED! The BEST Remote Junior Client Success Manager In The World

To apply, answer the questions in the application form. One of them asks you to type exactly: "I actually read the instructions."

Most account managers forward emails and read reports out loud on calls. We are not looking for that person. Our clients are doctors who own cash-pay medical clinics. We are looking for the person they call first: the one who spots the problem before they do, tells them before they ask, and shows up with the fix already moving.

Who we are: a US-based growth consultancy for cash-pay medical practices. Our website says it plainly: marketing agencies suck, so we built Guidepost to be the exception. We run Meta and Google ads into funnels built in GoHighLevel, and every piece of work ties back to one question: did the clinic make money? You would join a pod (a CSM, a small, lean team with shared support) that owns clients end to end. Monthly client churn is under 1%.
attributes.functions:
• You own the relationship. The doctor emails you, Slacks you and gets on calls with you.
  • You turn requests into work. Every client ask becomes a ClickUp task the team can act on without a follow-up question, with the why attached. "Build a new landing page" is not a brief. "The heatmap shows people stop scrolling before the CTA, so the CTA moves above the fold" is. When it is something you can build, you build it.
  • You narrate the numbers. In two minutes, in plain English: what is working, what is not, and what is next.
  • You catch problems first. The client never discovers an issue we have not already told them about.
  • You spot the next win. Not a pitch. Arithmetic out loud with the client's own numbers until the next step is obvious.

This is not a messenger seat: from day one you also build GoHighLevel automations, workflows and landing pages, using AI to move fast. And if all you do on a call is read a report, you are not doing the job.

What a good month looks like

  • Every client request became a ClickUp task with enough context that nobody had to come back to you to ask what it meant.
  • You ran the client calls yourself. The CEO was not on them.
  • You built or fixed automations, workflows or pages yourself instead of leaving them in someone else's queue.
  • Your pod's daily client updates went out accurate, because you read them before they shipped and corrected the one that was wrong.
  • No client surprised anyone with a problem, and no client cancelled without the risk being visible weeks earlier.
  • You brought at least one expansion case built on a client's real numbers, or explained why the timing was wrong.

How we work

  • Reply to clients within 1 business hour, even if it is "got it, looking into it," with a real answer or a timeline within 24. Reply to internal Slack within 10 minutes.
  • Decisions live on the ClickUp task or in the client channel. Never in DMs.
  • Monday all-hands, 9:00 to 10:30 AM Eastern.
attributes.benefits:
• Junior Client Success Managers start at $1,500 USD per month, plus a share of the pod's monthly bonus pool.
  • Raises follow responsibility, not tenure. And a 90-day review with the CEO to set what comes next.
  • CSM to Strategist. This is a real step people here have been offered.
  • Earn more by carrying more. Cover more than one seat in your pod well and you earn more than one seat's share of the bonus.
  • Learn a niche most marketers never touch. Doctors as clients, four- and five-figure treatments. People who get good at this are rare, and they get paid like it.
  • Room to build, zero micromanagement. See a better way to run things? Say so and run it.

Terms: full-time independent contractor, paid semi-monthly in USD. 20 days of paid time off a year, including six US holidays, approved in advance. Fourteen-day notice, either party. Location flexible, Eastern hours fixed.

About CoreVenture Exteriors

CoreVenture Exteriors is a fast-growing residential roofing, gutter, and exterior contractor focused on high-end new construction homes in the Denver metro area. Our remote operations team supports Colorado field crews and builder partners through our documented systems, clear expectations, and consistent execution. We want someone who will grow with us, not simply fill a seat.

About This Role

The Assistant Coordinator keeps projects moving through dependable administrative and operational support. You will start by mastering a defined set of recurring responsibilities, then grow into broader project coordination as the company expands. No roofing experience is required; we provide training. What matters is noticing problems before anyone asks: completed work that has not been billed, missing project information, or a crew without what it needs tomorrow. We are hiring for initiative, attention to detail, and the drive to take ownership and follow through.
attributes.functions:
Project quality review
Check projects against quality standards. Record incomplete work, missing documentation, and deviations in our project system. Notify responsible parties the same day and track issues to closure.

Customer and builder billing
Maintain records, confirm invoice receipt and approval status, and follow up on balances and payment dates, mainly by email with occasional calls. Escalate concerns to the Director of Operations. Use a service-first tone, not pressure.

Vendor invoices and payables
Check invoices against orders, deliveries, and pricing. Route for approval, process approved invoices, resolve vendor discrepancies, and keep audit-ready records.

Weekly reporting
Deliver accurate, timely reports on work orders, completion, billing, and open balances. Maintain weekly consistency and highlight patterns.

Crew and field coordination
Coordinate schedules, sequencing, and daily logistics. Confirm crews have information, materials, and documentation before starting. Communicate schedule, weather, and scope changes promptly. Be a reliable field contact during working hours. Much of this communication is in Spanish.

As needed
Support licensing and permitting; document and improve processes.

Phase 2: Grow into ownership
Master the fundamentals, then train as full backup to the Project Coordinator. Progress toward independent ownership of scheduling, material procurement, warranties, builder communication, and job execution. The goal is to master the operation, not remain an assistant. Growth depends on your progress.

Success milestones
30 days: Know systems and workflows, deliver accurate reports on time, and keep billing records current.
60 days: Handle vendor invoices, billing follow-up, and quality reviews independently; build crew relationships.
90 days: Cover the Project Coordinator's core duties without supervision and propose one concrete improvement to a process you own.

We run two products: a supplement brand (e-commerce, US market) and a self-improvement app (subscription). Both are launched, both have paying customers. We need one person to run paid acquisition, hands-on, working directly with the founder.
What you will do:

  • Research competitor ads (Meta Ad Library, TikTok Creative Center) and turn what works into new angles and hooks
  • Own creative strategy with the founder: which angles to test, why, in what order - you bring proposals, we decide fast, you execute faster

attributes.projects:
Stealth Seller is a product for Amazon resellers. Our users buy from Walmart, Target and Sam's Club and resell on Amazon. We give them the data to know what is worth buying.
We are three people. One founder, two engineers. The product is live, has paying customers, and ships every week.
Why this role exists
Nobody here owns product discovery. The founder decides what to build from memory, between writing code, so good ideas get lost and the roadmap is whatever he remembers.
This role is the listening half of product management. You own the question of what we build next and you defend the answer. You run discovery, find the pattern in what users say, and build the ranked list the engineers work from.
Talking to customers is how you get that signal, so you will live in Intercom and on calls. That is the input, not the job.
The founder makes the final call on what ships, because at three people he is the one building it. Do this well and those calls become yours.
attributes.functions:
Product. What we build next.

  • Own the weekly priority list. Ranked, with the reason behind each item. The founder approves it in 15 minutes on Monday.
  • Turn scattered requests into decisions. What matters, what waits, what we never build.
  • Write tickets clear enough that our engineers never ask a follow-up question.
  • Keep our project board actually accurate. Today it is not.
  • Test features when they ship and close the loop with whoever asked for it.
Discovery. Where the signal comes from.

  • Run 3 to 5 customer calls a week. Record them, write the notes, find the pattern.
  • Own Intercom. You are the first response to every customer message, every day. This is where most of the signal lives.
  • Collect every request from every channel into one place.
Communication. Telling people what changed.

  • Write and send release notes when we ship. Our users should never discover a feature by accident.
  • Own downtime and incident communication. When something breaks, you tell people what happened and when it is fixed.
  • Write and maintain our help docs.
  • Update marketing copy and write blog pages as the product changes.
  • Help us find users outside our current channel.
How you ramp. We are three people. You will be useful in week two, not month three.
  • Week 1. You listen. Sit in every internal call, read every Intercom thread, ask a huge amount of questions. Being annoying with questions is the job.
  • Week 2. You shadow the founder. You answer Intercom with him reviewing, and write your first release notes.
  • Week 3 to 4. Intercom is yours. You run your first customer calls.
  • Month 2. The weekly priority list is yours.
  • Month 3 and on. Help docs, marketing and blog open up.

  • Real ownership of an area, not a piece of someone else's process.
Compensation

  • USD $1,200 to $1,600 per month, based on experience.
How to apply

Send your application through Get on Board. In your cover letter, answer one question:
Tell us about a time you changed what a team was building because of something a customer told you. What did they say, and what did you do with it?

We read every one. Generic applications will not be read past the first line.
